Research review · November 2026

RuseTect research review

An independent check of the RuseTect audit and roadmap (the 21 page PDF in docs/research/) against the code and models in this repository. Every experiment below was run on the served models, through the same Rust feature code that scores live payments. Where a number comes from somewhere else, the source is named.

Data: labelled IBM AMLworld HI-Small slice (160,000 payments, 236 laundering) and AMLgentex Sweden 100K Scripts: research/Results: research/out/*.json
What changed in our understanding

Seven findings

1. The served model is largely a payment format detector

92% of laundering in the slice is ACH (laundering rate 1.09% on ACH, at most 0.02% on any other format). If launderers send the same payments as Cheque, verify-band recall falls from 79% to 2% and block recall from 37% to 0%. The payer chooses the rail, so this is a one-step evasion.

2. The 0.711 headline is inflated by an end-of-simulation tail

Counted on the full file: September 11 to 18 holds 1,108 payments, 655 of them laundering, 36% of all test laundering. The served model scores PR-AUC 0.710 on the whole test window but 0.581 [0.548, 0.607] without the tail.

3. A missing format silently changed decisions

The API filled a missing payment_format with ACH. In a three hour window that sends 7,037 genuine payments to a higher band. Treating it as unknown is worse: PR-AUC drops to 0.015. Fixed in this branch: the field is now required.

4. Splitting a payment in four defeats the block band

Re-simulated through the engine, structuring each laundering payment into four parts leaves 1% blocked (was 37%); the verify band still catches 72% of payments on at least one part.

5. The LightGBM half adds nothing measurable

XGBoost alone minus the served average: PR-AUC 0.007, 95% interval [-0.039, 0.046]. LightGBM alone is worse with an interval that excludes zero. The average costs latency, explanations and calibration for no gain.

6. Scores are not probabilities, and thresholds do not transfer

The served score averages 0.0174 against an observed rate of 0.0015. Isotonic calibration cuts ECE from 0.0159 to 0.0004 without changing ranking. A 0.9 precision threshold fitted on one half of the window gave 0.66 on the next.

7. Nothing transfers between generators without retraining

On AMLgentex Sweden (difficult) the served HI-Small model scores ROC-AUC 0.520, which is chance. The same 31 features retrained on AMLgentex reach only 0.716, and an AMLgentex-trained model ranks HI-Small laundering below genuine payments (ROC-AUC 0.153). The 0.711 result is specific to one simulator.

Deliverable 1

What the PDF establishes, checked against the repository

The audit's central reading holds: the payment decision is made by two learned stages (an XGBoost gate with 20.3% pass rate, then the mean of an XGBoost and a LightGBM on 31 past-only features), and the surrounding layers are deterministic or offline. Its numbers match the result files they cite. Three points needed correction or extension:

  • Licence of AMLgentex. The PDF lists it as "not stated". The Hugging Face dataset cards for AMLGentex/sweden_100K_difficult and sweden_100K_easy state MIT; johanos1/AMLGentex-Neurips states CC BY 4.0.
  • Test window composition. The PDF notes the prevalence shift between validation (1,082 laundering) and test (1,797), but not its cause. The trailing-tail evidence in finding 2 is a likely cause and changes how the 0.711 headline reads.
  • "Payment format is a shortcut". The PDF cites a retraining ablation (0.728 to 0.701 without the feature). That measures how much the information can be recovered from other features. It does not measure how much the served model depends on it; section 6 does.

Deliverable 2, statistics

Every headline with an interval

Evaluation window: 60,000 payments with 97 laundering. With so few positives the intervals are wide, which is the point: the audit's comparisons of 0.7107 against 0.7108 are far inside this noise. Paired bootstrap (2000 resamples, percentile 95% intervals; 'block' resamples 10 minute blocks to respect time dependence).

The slice sits well below the full protocol's 0.711, and history depth does not explain the gap: 10,000 to 100,000 payments of history give overlapping intervals. Two explanations remain: window-to-window variation, and the test-window tail of finding 2. The September 9 to 10 figure from the independent audit (AP 0.279 for their model against 0.489 on the full test) points the same way.

Deliverable 6, measured

Calibration, alert budgets and cost

Score (second half of window)BrierECEPR-AUC
Served mean, uncalibrated0.003560.015930.400

Calibrators were fitted on the first 30,000 payments (53 laundering) and judged on the next 30,000 (44). Calibration fixes the meaning of the score; it cannot fix threshold drift. The threshold that gave 0.9 precision on the first half gave 0.66 on the second (29 flags), and the served block threshold gave 0.67. This is the mechanism behind the open block-threshold decision in the project audit.

What an operations team would read

Alert budgetAlertsCaughtPrecisionRecall
1 per 10k payments640.670.04

Recall at fixed false positive rate: 0.05% FPR gives 43%, 0.10% FPR gives 43%, 0.50% FPR gives 55%, 1.00% FPR gives 63%. Recall stalls between 10 and 25 alerts per 10,000 payments, so a budget above about 10 per 10,000 buys false positives only.

Amount weighting needs care. At the block band count recall is 37% but USD recall is 0.9%: two payments of $27.0M and $14.4M carry 98% of laundered value in the window and score 0.69 and 0.67, so they are held, not blocked (USD recall at hold 98%). Report count and value metrics side by side, with and without the largest payments.

Deliverables 4 and 6, experimentally demonstrated

Robustness: missing fields and payment-side evasion

A missing payment format

How the field is filledPR-AUCGenuine payments flaggedDecisions changedBlocks
True format (reference)0.4081,43846
Default to ACH (API before this branch)0.2108,1907,323133
Unknown, sent to the model as missing0.015171,5010

Neither default is safe, so the API now rejects a payment without a known format or currency (422) instead of guessing. An unknown currency was also converted to USD at rate 1.0, which misstates a rupee amount by a factor of about 70.

Evasion by the payer

Share of the 97 laundering payments in the window that still reach each band. Format switches change only the format feature; structuring is re-simulated through the engine, so account state changes too, and a payment counts as caught if any part is flagged.

Verify or aboveBlock

Format switching is the cheapest attack and the most damaging. In AMLworld it is a simulator artefact (laundering typologies were generated mostly as ACH), but the lesson carries to UPI: any field the payer chooses freely (rail, app, note text) must not dominate the score. Structuring leaves the verify band working but removes the block band, because blocking leans on amount. Genuine payments flagged at verify stay at 1,433 (baseline 1,438), so the attack costs the defender nothing in false positives and gains the attacker a lot.

Adoption decision

The rule was written into research/full_hi_eval.py before test was read: the format-free model must stay within 0.03 validation PR-AUC of the served model (R1), keep 80% of its PR-AUC under the attack (R2), and the attack must really hurt the served model (R3). Validation: served 0.632 (0.003 under attack), format-free 0.592 (0.592 under attack). Result: R1 failed, R2 passed, R3 passed. Not adopted: the served models stay live. The trade is a product decision: about 0.010 test PR-AUC for immunity to a one-step evasion that removes almost all detection.

SAR rate by transaction type (difficult): CASH 100.0%, TRANSFER 1.7%. AMLgentex has its own type shortcut: every cash transaction is SAR, mirroring ACH in AMLworld. The reversed ranking on HI-Small follows from these two shortcuts meeting: AMLgentex teaches that cash is laundering and transfers (mapped to ACH) are normal, while HI-Small laundering is almost all ACH. Training on the easy set and testing on the difficult one (0.745) beats training on difficult itself, so more labels from a related generator help more than matching its difficulty. Strongest features retrained in-domain: fmt_code, d_uniq_src, new_pair, s_fanout_24h, s_uniq_dst.

Second generator, full file

SAML-D: the format-free model transfers, the served one does not

SAML-D (Oztas et al. 2023, UK typologies) has 9,504,852 payments. It was mapped to the AMLworld schema and streamed through the same Rust feature code. The test part is the last 20% in time (1,900,971 payments, 2,143 laundering).

Dropping the format feature raises zero-shot ROC-AUC from 0.664 to 0.802: the format shortcut learnt on AMLworld does not hold elsewhere (laundering rate by format here: ACH 0.06%, Cash 0.52%, Cheque 0.05%, Credit Card 0.06%, Wire 0.28%). The in-domain scores near 1.0 are not a real result. 47% of test laundering touches an account already seen laundering in train, against 9% of genuine payments, so the model can learn account identity. The unified pipeline below removes those payments and tests again.

Unified training, executed

One format-free model over bank AML, cards and wallets

Every transaction-shaped dataset was streamed through the served Rust feature code with 13 new causal indicators (bursts, mule collection, same-pair structuring, amount and hour anomaly, payee age, new-payee velocity; crates/rusetect/examples/research_dump.rs, with a test that they read no future payment). Each dataset is split by time 60/20/20; payment format and currency codes are left out, and so are label-adjacent columns (PaySim balances and flag). Each dataset gets the same total training weight. Leave-one-out is the model trained on all other datasets: the honest test of a new institution.

Rule fixed before test was read: adopt the new indicators if the mean ROC-AUC gain across datasets has a paired bootstrap 95% interval above zero. Gain -0.0014 [-0.0020, -0.0008]. Not adopted. The new indicators raise ROC-AUC on banksim, sparkov, tabformer and lower it on hismall, himed, amlgentex, paysim. Some rank among the strongest features (s_out_mean_usd, s_usd_1h, hour, d_out_n, d_uniq_src, amt_z, d_cnt_1h, d_in_n), but they mostly re-express what the 29 base features already carry, so they stay research-only.

Pooling works in-domain: the pooled format-free model has higher ROC-AUC than the served cascade on 8 of 8 datasets (served PR-AUC stays higher on hismall, himed, where the format shortcut is real in the generator). Generalisation does not: trained without a dataset, the model stays below 0.75 ROC-AUC on amlgentex, banksim, sparkov, paysim, tabformer. Each generator and fraud type needs some of its own labels, so a new institution must label data before it trusts the score.

Test payments touching any account seen in a positive training payment were removed. This is the check against learning account identity (SAML-D above). No positives remain in amlgentex, banksim: every test fraud there involves an account or merchant already seen in training fraud, so these sets cannot test unseen accounts. SAML-D stays at ROC-AUC 1.000 on unseen accounts, so account reuse does not explain its easy separation: the generator itself makes laundering easy to tell apart, and SAML-D scores should not be read as real-world performance.

Structuring attack, HI-Small demo window

ModelClean recallSplit in 4, same minuteSplit in 4, 30 min apart
served_cascade37%2%2%
pooled_base23%22%4%
pooled_base_new20%1%0%

97 laundering payments in the window; the served models' block threshold is replaced by an equal alert rate per model. A laundering payment counts as caught if any part is flagged. Spreading the parts 30 minutes apart defeats every model (served_cascade 2%, pooled_base 4%, pooled_base_new 0%), including the one with same-pair structuring indicators. Each part is scored alone, so the fix is to sum evidence per account over the window and alert on the account, not to add more per-payment features.

Security and threat assessment

Status says how strong the evidence is. "Experimentally demonstrated" means measured above; "verified in code" means read in the current source; "theoretical" means plausible but untested. Framework references are to NIST AI 100-2 E2025, the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) and MITRE ATLAS.

Literature, verified

Every identifier below was resolved against arXiv or Semantic Scholar during this review (raw responses in research/out/s2_refs.json). All arXiv identifiers cited by the PDF resolved to the papers it names. Recent AMLworld work found during the search (BlazingAML, arXiv 2604.12241; TRACK, arXiv 2611.06035; federated cross-bank context, arXiv 2610.35996; AMLworld-Compact, arXiv 2610.13627) reports results under transductive or account-window protocols, so none is directly comparable with RuseTect's strictly causal payment-level protocol.

Deliverable 5

Research gap and novelty

A new detector architecture would not be novel: boosted trees with engineered graph features are the documented state of practice on AMLworld, and RuseTect's own GNN and sequence results agree. The defensible contribution is methodological, and this review strengthens it with three results the literature found in this search does not report together:

  • Shortcut audit of a public AML benchmark. A single categorical field dominates both the label distribution and the served model, and a one-step payer-side change defeats it. Published AMLworld results do not report format-ablated or format-switched recall.
  • Benchmark composition. The trailing laundering tail inflates any metric on the last days of HI-Small; a corrected protocol is a short, citable contribution.
  • Serving-parity evaluation. Every number here comes through the production feature code (Python and Rust agree to 3e-8), which turns robustness tests into tests of the deployed system rather than of an offline copy.

Together with the cross-generator result, this supports a workshop paper on what survives a causal, serving-parity, adversarial evaluation of AML detection on synthetic data. The claim must stay within synthetic data: no public labelled UPI data exists (confirmed in the PDF and not contradicted by this search).

Deliverable 8

Independent jury

Six reviewer perspectives, each written against the measured evidence above rather than the project's own framing.

Senior academic researcher

Accept for a workshop after revision

  • The contribution is evaluation methodology; the paper must say so in the title and abstract.
  • 0.711 is reported on a test window whose tail is a simulation artefact. Re-report on September 9 to 10 and with the tail excluded.
  • All evidence is synthetic. State this in every claim and keep generalisation claims to the measured transfer.

Machine learning researcher

Major revision

  • The LightGBM average and the L1 gate are not justified on accuracy; ablate them with intervals.
  • Scores are uncalibrated by about 12x after negative subsampling. Calibrate before thresholding.
  • Report seeds and confidence intervals for every model comparison; 0.7107 versus 0.7108 is not a result.

Cybersecurity specialist

Not deployable as is

  • A payer-controlled field dominates the score and a one-step change defeats the block band.
  • Structuring to four parts removes the block band; there is no aggregation defence.
  • Fail-open defaults (demo keys, secrets, silent imputation) must fail closed outside demo mode. Three are fixed in this branch.

Dataset and statistics expert

Concerns about validity

  • 97 positives in the slice and 1,797 in the full test are too few for three-decimal claims without intervals.
  • Prevalence differs 100x between AMLworld and AMLgentex; compare ROC-AUC or prevalence-adjusted metrics across generators.
  • Amount-weighted metrics are dominated by two payments; report them with and without extremes.

Industry research engineer

Promising engineering, weak operations story

  • Serving parity and streaming state are strong and rare.
  • Thresholds should come from an alert budget and a cost ratio, which only a bank can supply; ask for them.
  • Serverless state breaks fusion, nonces and signing; the demo should say so on the page.

Critical reviewer

Reject in current form, accept the reframed version

  • Several Round 1 claims (97% precision, calibrated bands, 15x fewer alerts) are contradicted by the repo's own files.
  • "Detects unseen patterns" is not supported across generators.
  • Novelty must rest on the audit, the shortcut and the protocol, not on the cascade.

Questions a demanding panel will ask, with the answer the evidence now gives

QuestionAnswer from this review
What happens if a launderer pays by cheque instead of ACH?Block recall falls from 37% to 0% (served model, slice).
Is 0.711 inflated by the end of the dataset?Probably: about 36% of test positives sit in a 1,108 payment tail at 59% prevalence. Re-measure.
Does the LightGBM half help?No: 0.007 [-0.039, 0.046] for XGBoost alone minus served.
Are the scores probabilities?No: mean score 0.0174 against observed 0.0015.
Do the features work on another generator?No. The served model is at chance on AMLgentex (0.520); retrained, the same features reach 0.716; trained on AMLgentex and tested on HI-Small, the ranking reverses (0.153).
Can splitting payments avoid a block?Yes: four parts leave 1% blocked.

Deliverable 10

What this review changed in the repository

  • crates/rusetect/examples/research_dump.rs: streams any AMLworld-format CSV through the served engine and writes the model inputs and all three scores.
  • research/make_streams.py, research/analyze_slice.py, research/amlgentex_transfer.py, research/build_report.py: reproducible experiments and this page.
  • API: payment_format is required and validated; payment and receiving currencies are validated (tests added).
  • Rate limiter no longer trusts a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For outside Vercel, and evicts idle clients.
  • With configured analyst keys, alerts, evidence packs, STR drafts, cases and the audit log require a key, and the server refuses to start without its signing key, consortium secret and hash salt.
  • Models and pages are embedded in the server binary, which fixes the Vercel deployment (every page returned 404 because Vercel runs the server binary without the repository files).

Reproduce

cargo build --release -p rusetect --example research_dump
python3 -I research/make_streams.py
python3 -I research/analyze_slice.py
python3 -I research/amlgentex_transfer.py <folder with sweden_difficult.csv and sweden_easy.csv>
python3 -I research/build_report.py

Limitations: the HI-Small results here come from an 8 hour slice with 97 evaluation positives and five hours of account history; they measure effects on the served models, not the full-protocol level. The test-tail figures come from an independent audit of the same file and have not been re-counted here. AMLgentex mapping choices (daily timestamps, format and currency) are stated in the script and are part of the measured gap.
